text:
Maya: FYI ACME's trial POC is hitting repeated 429s on /v1/generate even though the token budget in the console shows ~40% used. Started ~09:15 PT during load testing. Demo is tomorrow — can eng swarm?

Devin: Can you paste a sample request ID + any x-* headers you see? Is it per-route cap or tenant-wide?

acme-dev: sample curl below, plus raw 429 response headers we captured. We see Retry-After: 2 and some x-rate-* headers.

acme-dev: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"summary of docs","stream":false}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-ID: rq_0a1b2c3d
Retry-After: 2
X-Redwood-Route-Limit: 10000
X-Redwood-Route-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Tenant-Burst: 15000
X-Redwood-Tenant-Remaining: 5000
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"route token burst exceeded"}
```

Maya: @Devin @Ryan - note the Route-Remaining shows 0 even though tenant remaining is nonzero. They haven't changed config lately.

Ryan: Looks like classic burst-window exhaustion on the route. Tenant has spare tokens but the per-route burst bucket is drained. Are they sending lots of short concurrent requests?

acme-dev: yes, our client fires ~12 concurrent small requests for UI cards on page load. Each request is ~120 tokens.

Devin: That pattern can hit the per-route burst even if overall token use is fine. Our accounting charges each request's tokens against the route bucket and concurrent bursts are limited by a short window. Two quick checks: (1) check the route config in Console -> Usage -> Route caps, (2) confirm whether streaming vs non-streaming affects billing for them (streaming may have smaller initial token billing).

Lina: For an urgent demo, we can do a temporary route cap bump for 24h. Otherwise recommend client-side concurrency throttle (3) + exponential backoff (jitter). Also consider prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Alex: @acme-dev can you paste the tenant_id and the exact route name? I'll prepare an approval request for a temporary bump and include cost estimate.

acme-dev: tenant_id: tn_acme_77, route: /v1/generate (model=open-7b). request_id from failing call: rq_0a1b2c3d.

Devin: I pulled traces for rq_0a1b2c3d. Pattern: 11 requests in a 12-second window, each ~120 tokens => ~1320 tokens in window. Route burst configured to 1000 tokens/10s (effective), so it tripples. Two mitigation paths: 1) temp bump route burst to 3000 tokens/10s, 2) reduce client concurrency to 3 and add 200ms jitter which keeps peak under the route limit. Either works for demo.

Maya: Can we do a 24h bump to 3000 tokens/10s? Demo at 13:00 PT. Lina, you OK to approve emergency bump?

Lina: :thumbsup: Approving 24h bump to 3000/10s for tn_acme_77. Ops to apply and monitor. Please log the change for post-mortem.

Ryan: Applying now. I'll insert the temp override and add a dashboard alert for route remaining < 20%. ETA ~5m. Applying change for route `/v1/generate` on tenant tn_acme_77.

deploy-bot: change-request tn_acme_77:route-bump -> APPROVED by Lina (solutions-eng). Change ID: cr_8821.

Ryan: Done. Route cap bump active. Monitoring link: https://console.redwood.example/tenants/tn_acme_77/usage/route/v1%2Fgenerate/alerts (will keep an eye for anomalies).

acme-dev: Confirming — after bump and we throttled client concurrency to 3 with 150-300ms jitter, 429s disappeared. Demo went well, thanks everyone.

Devin: Follow-ups: (A) we should add a console hint about common UI patterns (many small concurrent requests) and recommend concurrency defaults, (B) consider auto-increase grace for short demo windows for trial tenants, (C) log the post-mortem and add to KB.

Maya: I'll own the post-mortem doc and send the cost estimate to ACME. Great work team. :tada:
